new_statements.quote: [p. 46, Summary] The Ikema dialect of Miyako, Southern Ryukyuan, has a three-pattern accent system in which three tone classes (Types A, B, and C) are lexically contrastive, although the Type A simplex nouns are fewer. [p. 46] 池間方言は，語の長さが増えてもアクセント型の対立数が増加せず，その対立数が 3 である三型アクセント体系（上野 1984, 2012）を有する。[...] 三型アクセント体系を有する宮古語諸方言には，池間方言のほかに，多良間方言（松森 2010），与那覇方言（松森 2013），狩俣方言（松森 2015）がある [p. 50] 非中和環境において，2 番目の韻律語と 3 番目の韻律語の双方に高ピッチが現れない型を A 型，2 番目の韻律語に高ピッチが現れず 3 番目の韻律語に高ピッチが現れる型を B 型，2 番目の韻律語に高ピッチが現れるが 3 番目の韻律語に高ピッチが現れない型を C 型と定義し，議論を進める。
new_statements.translation: [p. 46] The Ikema dialect does not increase its number of contrasting accent types as words get longer; it has a three-pattern accent system (Uwano 1984, 2012) with three contrasts. [...] Besides Ikema, the Miyako dialects with a three-pattern accent system include Tarama (Matsumori 2010), Yonaha (Matsumori 2013) and Karimata (Matsumori 2015). [p. 50] In non-neutralizing environments we define as Type A the pattern in which high pitch appears on neither the second nor the third prosodic word, as Type B the pattern in which high pitch does not appear on the second prosodic word but does on the third, and as Type C the pattern in which high pitch appears on the second prosodic word but not on the third, and proceed on that basis.

new_statements.rule_in_words: No word stress is described. Ikema Miyako has a three-way lexically contrastive tone-class (N-pattern 'accent') system: every noun belongs to Type A, B or C, and the class is realized as a distribution of high pitch over prosodic words in the phrase, not at a fixed position in the word. Prosodic words are built by rule (1), p. 47: 'insert a prosodic-word boundary at the left edge of every root or clitic of two or more moras' (one-mora clitics fuse with the preceding prosodic word). The three-way contrast is neutralized in most short environments and surfaces only when the phrase contains three (or more) prosodic words or is followed by a predicate; Type A high pitch falls on neither the 2nd nor the 3rd prosodic word, Type B on the 3rd, Type C on the 2nd. Type A simplex nouns are rare (about 5%, 6 of 121 nouns) because of a historical merger of A into B.
new_statements.exceptions: 4-mora simplex nouns keep the three-way contrast even in a two-prosodic-word phrase (5b, p. 50); older descriptions (Hirayama 1964, 1983; Hirayama et al. 1967; Sakimura 2006; Hayashi et al. 2008) wrongly gave Ikema a two-pattern system (p. 46); speakers tend to put phonetic prominence on an utterance-final clitic (especially =mai), which obscures the accent contrast (pp. 50-51); Type A nouns that share particular meanings (numbers, people, time, space, place names) resisted the A>B merger (sec. 3-4).
new_statements.identity_note: Work 1's substitute (Igarashi 2016) describes the Ikema dialect of Miyako, with all data recorded in the Nishihara settlement of Miyakojima (Ikema is spoken on Ikema island, in Sarahama on Irabu, and in Nishihara on Miyakojima), p. 46. Work 0 concerns Tarama (Tarama island), a distinct Miyako variety, not opened. The statement that Tarama, Yonaha and Karimata are also three-pattern systems is Igarashi's citation of Matsumori, not a direct reading of those sources. Earlier on-disk files in the same directory (Shimoji 2009 on Irabu, Pellard 2009 on Ogami, Igarashi et al. 2012 on Ikema) were downloaded by an earlier reading and were not in this task's works list, so they were not re-read here.

tone_statements.quote: その結果、皆愛方言のアクセント体系は 3 種類のアクセント型が区別されると分析しなければならない。... 音調（高音調・低音調）付与の単位は拍である。... 以上、各アクセント型の解釈をまとめると、次のようになる。• c 型は 1 つ目の韻律語に下げ核を持つ。• b 型は 2 つ目の韻律語に下げ核を持つ。• a 型は無核である。• 下げ核は指定される韻律語の末尾境界から数えて 3 拍目に位置する。さらに、皆愛方言のプロソディーを記述するために、次のような記述を加える必要がある。• 文節の初頭拍に句境界の高音調が義務的に挿入される。• 文節の初頭拍に挿入される高音調は下げ核が結びつく直前の拍まで右へと拡張する。• 文節が無核である場合、接語によって形成される最初の韻律語に下げ核が付与される。• 高音調と下げ核が同じ拍に結びつくと、下げ核が次の拍に移動する。
tone_statements.translation: As a result, the accent system of the Minaai dialect must be analysed as distinguishing three accent types. ... The unit of tone (high tone / low tone) assignment is the mora. ... Summing up the interpretation of each accent type: type c has a lowering kernel in the 1st prosodic word; type b has a lowering kernel in the 2nd prosodic word; type a is kernel-less (unaccented); the lowering kernel is located on the 3rd mora counted from the final boundary of the specified prosodic word. Further, to describe Minaai prosody: a phrase-boundary high tone is obligatorily inserted on the initial mora of the bunsetsu; this high tone spreads rightward up to the mora just before the one the lowering kernel links to; if the bunsetsu is kernel-less, a lowering kernel is assigned to the first prosodic word formed by a clitic; when the high tone and the lowering kernel link to the same mora, the kernel moves to the next mora.

tone_statements.quote: 南琉球宮古語池間方言の3種類のアクセントの違いは、語を単独で発音しても、助詞を付けて発音しても、観察できない。池間方言のアクセントは語に2拍以上の助詞と述語を後続させると、もっとも明瞭に観察できる。3種類のアクセントは語の外側で実現される声の高さで区別される。語を超えて実現されるアクセントを正確にとらえるためには音響分析が有効。 ... 池間方言にもアクセントがある。 ... 「西-も ない」 A型 ... 「錐-も ない」 B型 ... 「海-も ない」 C型
tone_statements.translation: The differences among the three kinds of accent of the Ikema dialect of Miyako, Southern Ryukyuan, cannot be observed when a word is pronounced in isolation, nor when it is pronounced with a particle attached. The accent of the Ikema dialect is observed most clearly when a particle of two or more moras and a predicate follow the word. The three kinds of accent are distinguished by the pitch realised outside the word. Acoustic analysis is effective for capturing accurately an accent realised beyond the word. ... The Ikema dialect too has accent. ... 'west-also not' Type A ... 'awl-also not' Type B ... 'sea-also not' Type C

tone_statements.quote: 多良間方言の名詞アクセントは最大 3 つの型が区別される三型体系を有する。3 つの型は，韻律句内におけるピッチの下降の有無と位置によって区別される（松森 2014；五十嵐 2015, 2016；青井 2016a, 2016d）。... 本稿では，表層形のピッチパターンから，3 つの型をそれぞれ下降 1 型（F1 型），下降 2 型（F2 型），平板型（F0 型）と呼ぶことにする ... アクセント核はモーラが担うが，その位置を決定するためにはモーラだけを参照するのでは不充分であり，韻律語も併せて参照する必要がある ... c. 音調付与規則 アクセント核が指定されたモーラまでは H 音調を付与し，それ以降のモーラには L 音調を付与せよ。
tone_statements.translation: Tarama noun accent has a three-pattern system in which at most three classes are distinguished. The three classes are distinguished by the presence/absence and position of a pitch fall within the prosodic phrase ... From the surface pitch patterns I call the three classes Falling-1 (F1), Falling-2 (F2) and Level (F0) ... The accent kernel is borne by the mora, but to determine its position it is not enough to refer to morae alone; the prosodic word must also be referred to ... c. Tone assignment rule: assign H tone up to the mora specified with the accent kernel and L tone to the morae after it.

tone_statements.quote: 多良間方言のアクセントは，3 つの型の区別（下降 1 型（F1），下降 2 型（F2），平板型（F0））をもつ三型体系である。3 つのアクセント型はピッチ下降の有無と位置によって弁別される。これら 3 つの型（特に 2 つの下降型）のピッチパターンは，2 モーラ以上の接語もしくは語根が写像される韻律単位，つまり韻律語（Prosodic Word）を仮定することで初めて一般化が可能になる。 ... アクセント核はモーラが担う。 ... c. 音調付与規則 アクセント核が指定されたモーラまでは H 音調を付与し，それ以降のモーラには L 音調を付与せよ。
tone_statements.translation: The accent of the Tarama dialect is a three-pattern system with a distinction of three types (falling type 1 (F1), falling type 2 (F2), level type (F0)). The three accent types are distinguished by the presence or absence and the position of a pitch fall. The pitch patterns of these three types (especially the two falling types) can be generalized only by positing the prosodic word, a prosodic unit onto which clitics or roots of two or more morae are mapped. ... The accent kernel is borne by the mora. ... c. Tone assignment rule: assign H tone up to the mora specified as the accent kernel, and L tone to the morae after it.

tone_statements.summary: Three lexical accent classes on roots (F1/F2: nucleus on 1st/2nd prosodic word of the phrase; F0 unaccented), realized H then L after the nucleus; the 3 units are accent classes; 60+ forms.

tone_statements.quote: この狩俣方言も、多良間島方言と同様、ピッチの下がり目の位置が有意味な体系である。... ここから、この狩俣方言も、三型アクセント体系を持っていることが分かった。... （11）宮古島の狩俣方言アクセントの仕組み （a）その体系内の３種の型のアクセントは、ピッチの下降の有無とその位置の違いによって区別される。（b）それぞれの型のアクセントは、次のように出現する。〈ａ型〉アクセントなし、〈ｂ型〉２つめのPWに出現、〈ｃ型〉最初のPWに出現 （c）下降は、原則的にそれぞれのPWの次末モーラに出現する。 また狩俣方言の具体的なピッチの出現は、（5）で論じた多良間島方言の音調付与規則と同じ規則によって予測できるものとする。
tone_statements.translation: This Karimata dialect too, like the Tarama-jima dialect, is a system in which the position of the pitch fall is significant. ... From this it became clear that this Karimata dialect also has a three-pattern accent system. ... (11) The mechanism of the accent of the Karimata dialect of Miyako Island: (a) the accents of the three types within the system are distinguished by the presence or absence of a pitch fall and by the difference in its position; (b) the accent of each type appears as follows: type a, no accent; type b, appears in the second PW; type c, appears in the first PW; (c) the fall appears, in principle, on the penultimate mora of the respective PW. Further, the concrete realisation of pitch in the Karimata dialect is taken to be predictable by the same rules as the tone-assignment rules of the Tarama-jima dialect discussed in (5).

tone_statements.translation: Matsumori (2001) and Matsumori (2010), on the basis of data like the following, pointed out that Tarama Island in the Miyako Islands, until then held to have a two-pattern accent system, has a three-pattern accent. ... (As to whether the Tarama dialect should be described as a 'tone' system, there is still too little to judge on and at present no decision can be made. ...) ... (28) Accent of the Tarama dialect (revised): Type a ... has a flat pitch pattern with no abrupt pitch fall anywhere in the phrase. Type b ...: an H tone appears in the second prosodic domain inside the phrase beginning with that word. Type c ...: an H tone appears in the first prosodic domain inside the phrase beginning with that word. ... (29) Position of the H tone in Tarama: the H tone is realised linked to the penultimate mora ([-2] mora) of each prosodic domain.

tone.translation: As a result, the accent system of the Minaai dialect must be analysed as distinguishing three accent types. ... The unit of tone (high tone / low tone) assignment is the mora. ... Summing up the interpretation of each accent type: type c has a lowering kernel in the 1st prosodic word; type b has a lowering kernel in the 2nd prosodic word; type a is kernel-less (unaccented); the lowering kernel is located on the 3rd mora counted from the final boundary of the specified prosodic word. Further, to describe Minaai prosody: a phrase-boundary high tone is obligatorily inserted on the initial mora of the bunsetsu; this high tone spreads rightward up to the mora just before the one the lowering kernel links to; if the bunsetsu is kernel-less, a lowering kernel is assigned to the first prosodic word formed by a clitic; when the high tone and the lowering kernel link to the same mora, the kernel moves to the next mora.

tone.translation: Tarama noun accent has a three-pattern system in which at most three classes are distinguished. The three classes are distinguished by the presence/absence and position of a pitch fall within the prosodic phrase ... From the surface pitch patterns I call the three classes Falling-1 (F1), Falling-2 (F2) and Level (F0) ... The accent kernel is borne by the mora, but to determine its position it is not enough to refer to morae alone; the prosodic word must also be referred to ... c. Tone assignment rule: assign H tone up to the mora specified with the accent kernel and L tone to the morae after it.

tone.translation: The accent of the Tarama dialect is a three-pattern system with a distinction of three types (falling type 1 (F1), falling type 2 (F2), level type (F0)). The three accent types are distinguished by the presence or absence and the position of a pitch fall. The pitch patterns of these three types (especially the two falling types) can be generalized only by positing the prosodic word, a prosodic unit onto which clitics or roots of two or more morae are mapped. ... The accent kernel is borne by the mora. ... c. Tone assignment rule: assign H tone up to the mora specified as the accent kernel, and L tone to the morae after it.

tone.translation: This Karimata dialect too, like the Tarama-jima dialect, is a system in which the position of the pitch fall is significant. ... From this it became clear that this Karimata dialect also has a three-pattern accent system. ... (11) The mechanism of the accent of the Karimata dialect of Miyako Island: (a) the accents of the three types within the system are distinguished by the presence or absence of a pitch fall and by the difference in its position; (b) the accent of each type appears as follows: type a, no accent; type b, appears in the second PW; type c, appears in the first PW; (c) the fall appears, in principle, on the penultimate mora of the respective PW. Further, the concrete realisation of pitch in the Karimata dialect is taken to be predictable by the same rules as the tone-assignment rules of the Tarama-jima dialect discussed in (5).

tone.translation: Matsumori (2001) and Matsumori (2010), on the basis of data like the following, pointed out that Tarama Island in the Miyako Islands, until then held to have a two-pattern accent system, has a three-pattern accent. ... (As to whether the Tarama dialect should be described as a 'tone' system, there is still too little to judge on and at present no decision can be made. ...) ... (28) Accent of the Tarama dialect (revised): Type a ... has a flat pitch pattern with no abrupt pitch fall anywhere in the phrase. Type b ...: an H tone appears in the second prosodic domain inside the phrase beginning with that word. Type c ...: an H tone appears in the first prosodic domain inside the phrase beginning with that word. ... (29) Position of the H tone in Tarama: the H tone is realised linked to the penultimate mora ([-2] mora) of each prosodic domain.

[p.87, §5] すなわち与那覇方言では，A 型は LLH，B 型は LHL，C 型は HLL という音調メロディーが，レキシコン内部において語彙項目ごとに指定されている，としなければならない。 また，単純語を使用しても，なかなか「3 型」までは見えてこなかった与那覇方言だが，複合語を使用すると，3 つの型の区別の存在がくっきりと浮き彫りになることも見てきた。 ... tone.translation: [p.85] From these facts it has become clear that the Yonaha dialect is a 'three-pattern system' consisting of three tonal patterns (LLH, LHL, HLL). ... [p.87] That is, in Yonaha the tonal melodies LLH for Type A, LHL for Type B and HLL for Type C must be taken to be specified item by item in the lexicon. We have also seen that, while the 'three patterns' hardly become visible with simplex words, the three-way distinction stands out sharply once compounds are used. ... [p.67, abstract] a constraint is involved whereby 'three morae form one unit, a foot, and the H tone is realised on that foot'.
